notes: The page carries manuscript page 5, archive pencil-like sheet number 13, and section 4. It is a typescript with machine x-outs, typed interlinear replacements, pen signs and underlines. No independent diagram or drawing was found.
The opening assumes a) and b) for the written morphism i_sbar: X_sbar -> X_sbar. Both X letters were read from the ink, without replacing the first by Y.

For a cycle z in Z^n(Y) whose fibre class is algebraically and hence cohomologically zero, the page says u(z) is defined in the indicated H^1 group and lies in the i-star image modulo torsion after possibly shrinking S.
The author qualifies the shrinking by "du moins" and calls it "restriction probablement inutile". The cancelled "sans doute" and live inserted "probablement" are both retained.

The proof invokes 2), a finite extension K/k(s), a trace argument, spreading the curve and cycle over S, and a decomposition z=i-star(z-prime)+z-double-prime. It asserts that the remaining class induces a zero fibre cohomology map and is zero by 1). These assertions were read, not independently proved.
The second paragraph invokes statements 1) and 2), but their contents are not supplied in this page packet. No theorem-level verification or background import was attempted.

The first cohomology display has two closing parentheses after n where the written nesting has three openings; the inline i-star group has three closing parentheses after n where its nesting has four openings. These source omissions are preserved, while LaTeX braces and math delimiters remain balanced.

The apparent self-map, the uncertain ambient product capitals, the coefficient correction and the final base/map letters were treated as diagnostic risks. Their crops were inspected; expected mathematics did not determine the transcription.

Section 4 introduces a smooth projective X of dimension m, adds "sur k Alg. clos," in pen, takes a Lefschetz pencil and writes a morphism from the blown-up X to P^1_k. It then chooses an open base and gives a final restriction map whose name/base/target remain partly uncertain.

No independent mathematical proof, computation, formal certificate, or use-and-recheck event was performed. check_events is intentionally empty; structural transcription checks are reported separately.

The base B is a literal first-candidate glyph reading, not a claim that B is the intended mathematical base. The subsequent B carries the earlier B/S/U/doubled-S uncertainty by the brief's recurring-glyph convention.
The extra x in the last display records visible cancellation ink after S. It is not asserted to have been part of the old mathematical target.
The extended ascender in fibres is treated as a retouch of b, not an independent letter, diagram, or marginal note. Its source layer is marked uncertain in place.
Structural alternatives involving deleted/live letters express uncertainty of temporal order; neither alternative is asserted unconditionally.
brief_feedback: The distinction between a visible overprint and its temporal old/live order is essential here. For future pages, an explicit neutral overprint convention would avoid forcing uncertain deletion-order alternatives. The base-letter repeat also shows why a preferred candidate must be labelled as a literal outline rather than an intended mathematical symbol.
